Name: Scientific Naturalism
Description: Worldview holding that natural laws govern all phenomena, the universe is self-contained, and scientific method is the primary path to knowledge.
CreationMyth: Approximately 13.8 billion years ago, the universe began in the Big Bang, an expansion from an infinitely dense singularity. Fundamental forces separated, particles formed, and after 380,000 years, atoms emerged. Gravity pulled matter into stars and galaxies. Heavy elements were forged in stellar cores and scattered by supernovae. 4.6 billion years ago, our solar system condensed from a molecular cloud. Earth formed through accretion and was bombarded by asteroids and comets that brought water. Around 3.8 billion years ago, self-replicating molecules emerged in Earth's primordial oceans. Through natural selection over billions of years, life evolved from single cells to complex multicellular organisms. Homo sapiens emerged in Africa around 300,000 years ago, developing culture, language, and eventually science to understand the cosmos.
CorePrinciples: Universe operates by natural laws, no supernatural intervention
Scientific method: observation, hypothesis, testing, revision
Evolution by natural selection explains life's diversity
Materialism: only physical matter and energy exist
Skepticism and evidence-based reasoning
Universe is indifferent to human concerns
Knowledge is provisional and subject to revision

Name: Transhumanism
Description: Intellectual movement advocating for using technology to enhance human physical and cognitive capabilities beyond current biological limitations.
CorePrinciples: Technology can and should enhance human capabilities
Death and suffering are problems to be solved, not accepted
Morphological freedom: right to modify one's body/mind
Technological singularity may radically transform existence
Intelligence explosion through AI possible
Life extension and immortality as goals
Rational scientific approach to human enhancement

Name: Deep Ecology
Description: Environmental philosophy emphasizing intrinsic value of all living beings and fundamental restructuring of human relationship with nature.
CorePrinciples: All life has intrinsic value independent of utility to humans
Ecological diversity and richness have value in themselves
Humans have no right to reduce biodiversity except to meet vital needs
Current human interference with nature is excessive
Fundamental change in economic, technological, and ideological structures needed
Self-realization through identification with all life
Ecocentric rather than anthropocentric worldview

Name: Effective Altruism
Description: Philosophical and social movement using evidence and reason to determine the most effective ways to benefit others and acting on that basis.
Sources: The Life You Can Save (Peter Singer)
CorePrinciples: Use evidence and reason to find the most effective ways to help others
Prioritize interventions by cost-effectiveness and scale
Equal moral consideration for all sentient beings
Earning to give: maximize income to donate effectively
Longtermism: consider impacts on future generations
Existential risk reduction as priority
Quantitative analysis of charitable impact

Name: Stoic Naturalism (Modern)
Description: Contemporary revival of Stoic philosophy integrated with scientific naturalism, emphasizing virtue, acceptance of nature, and rational living.
Sources: A Guide to the Good Life (William Irvine)
How to Be a Stoic (Massimo Pigliucci)
CorePrinciples: Focus on what's in your control, accept what isn't
Live according to nature and reason
Four cardinal virtues: wisdom, courage, justice, temperance
Negative visualization: contemplate loss to appreciate what you have
Dichotomy of control: distinguish internal from external
Amor fati: love of fate, embrace what happens
Cosmopolitanism: all humans are part of single community

Name: Integral Theory
Description: Comprehensive framework attempting to integrate insights from multiple disciplines and worldviews using developmental and systems perspectives.
CorePrinciples: AQAL framework: All Quadrants, All Levels, All Lines, All States, All Types
Developmental stages of consciousness
Integration of pre-modern, modern, and postmodern insights
Four quadrants: interior/exterior, individual/collective
Holarchy: nested hierarchies of increasing wholeness
Include and transcend: higher stages integrate lower ones
Multiple intelligences and developmental lines
